name: Mid-side EQ: center the bass, tame mid problems, widen with side mids/highs
goal: Use mid/side EQ on synth/sample/pad layers or mixes: split stereo into mid (L+R mono sum) and side (L−R), high-pass wide bass on the sides to focus low end center, cut resonant/harsh problems only on the mid when they live there, optionally boost the same band on the sides to preserve ambience, and try subtle upper-mid side boosts for depth (not only extreme high shelves for width).

source.title: Mid Side EQ Simplified - A Powerful Tool for Stereo Mixing

prerequisites: EQ with mid/side mode (or dual-mono M/S), headphones/monitors; basic EQ balance literacy

outputs.name: ms_eq_settings
outputs.description: Portable M/S EQ moves for pads/synths/mixes

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Do not always remove bass from sides — transcript notes stereo kick/side bass can be intentional; listen first.
Prefer smaller moves than dramatic YouTube demos; preserve what you can leave alone.

steps.action: Enable mid/side on the EQ. Confirm mid ≈ mono sum of L+R and side ≈ L minus R (spatial difference, not merely hard-panned parts).
If a synth/sample has overly wide bass: solo sides, high-pass the side channel to remove bass so sides keep ambience/air while lows become narrower and centered; A/B with full stereo.
steps.expect: Tighter, focused low end without killing side ambience

steps.action: If a lead/pad resonance is mostly mid-localized: solo mid vs side to locate it, then cut the problem band on the mid channel only.
steps.expect: Harshness reduced without flattening the whole stereo image

steps.action: Optionally boost a little top end on the sides after mid cuts so width/air remains; for mix problems where stereo EQ mushifies everything, cut only the mid band that holds the squeaky/scratchy energy (example: guitars in mid) and leave lush side reverb/ambience alone — even boost that same band on sides if you want air back.

For width/depth: try a subtle boost in the upper midrange on the sides (not only extreme high shelves) — transcript finds upper-mid side boosts create more depth/aliveness than highs-alone width tricks. Keep mastering-style moves modest.
steps.expect: Sensed depth/width without mono collapse disasters

verification: Side solo shows less bass after side HPF when focusing lows
Mid-only cuts fix harshness without dulling side reverb/ambience
Mono check still has solid centered low end
